info.name: AgentNexus FastAPI - Local Manual Test
info.description:
Documentation for the AgentNexus / Agent Saul development API.

## Start here
1. Set `baseUrl` to the API origin (default `http://localhost:5000`).
2. Register a disposable development account, verify its email, then run Login. Successful Login/Refresh tests save `access_token` and `refresh_token`.
3. Run health checks, upload a small supported fixture, poll ingestion status, then exercise search and Agent Saul.
4. Use an administrator token for admin/user/billing operations; use sandbox provider credentials for billing/webhooks.

## Collection scope
Contains 123 HTTP requests in 11 feature folders, including v1 compatibility and v2 routes. The checked-in OpenAPI snapshot `docs-site/openapi.json` supplies operation details where available; routes absent from it accept any 2xx status by default and should be cross-checked against the target server's `/swagger.json` if their contracts have changed.

## Variables and auth
Every collection variable has a description below. Keep real tokens/secrets local; use Postman local values or a private environment. Protected requests use Bearer `access_token`; public auth/health/root and provider webhook requests are explicitly unauthenticated. Crawler requests use Bearer auth.

## Tester quick start
1. Set `baseUrl` and create a private Postman environment for credentials, including separate `access_token` (regular user) and `admin_access_token` (admin) values.
2. Run one v2 flow at a time. In Auth, register, copy the verification token from the development email, verify, then log in.
3. IDs from successful create/list responses populate collection variables such as `doc_id`, `plan_id`, `subscription_id`, and `invoice_id`; inspect the variable after each create request.
4. For negative tests, set environment variable `allowClientError` to `true`; reset it to `false` for normal success testing. Destructive/state-changing requests are skipped unless `allowDestructive=true`.
5. For Razorpay, set `razorpayWebhookSecret` in the private environment. Its pre-request script signs the sample body.

## Request documentation
Tests expect each request’s documented 2xx status by default, so bad tokens and placeholder IDs fail instead of appearing to pass. For intentional negative cases, set `allowClientError=true` in a private Postman environment; 4xx status and error-envelope checks then apply.

Each request description documents its method and full variable-based URL, authentication, path/query parameters, headers, request body fields, documented response codes/media types, versioning, and the request test script. JSON bodies have `Content-Type: application/json`; multipart uploads have a `file` picker and must not set Content-Type manually.

## Safety and test assertions
Use development/sandbox services and disposable records. Never send production charges, refunds, destructive admin operations, or invalid webhook signatures to production. The shared test script only rejects 5xx responses and checks envelope status consistency; inspect each endpoint's expected status and persisted/background state manually. Agent Saul WebSocket, Celery workers, and scheduled work are covered in `docs/manual-testing-plan.md`.

## API versioning
v1 is deprecated (documented sunset `2027-06-15`). Use v2 for new integrations and verify v1 deprecation/successor headers when testing compatibility.

auth.description: Default Bearer auth uses `access_token`; administrator-only requests explicitly use `admin_access_token`. Public requests explicitly use no auth.

variable.description: API origin only, with no trailing slash. Change for local, staging, or another test server; keep the `/api/v1` or `/api/v2` prefix in each request URL.
Bearer access token. The login and refresh request tests populate this from successful token responses. Treat as a secret and do not commit or share a real value.
Refresh token used by refresh/logout requests. Login and refresh request tests update it. Treat as a secret.
Unique email address for a disposable, verified development account. Change before registration.
Password for the disposable test account. Use the policy-compliant development value; never use a real account password.
OAuth provider path value: `google` or `github`. A complete flow needs provider credentials and the signed state cookie.
Session ID returned by the sessions endpoint; not the Agent Saul thread ID.
Crawl ID returned by a successful crawl request.
User ID returned by an authorized user-list/read or account-creation flow.
Document ID returned by upload/ingestion. Use a document owned by the authenticated test user.
Plan ID returned by plan creation/listing in the billing sandbox.
Subscription ID returned by a successful sandbox subscription creation.
Payment ID returned by a sandbox subscription/payment flow.
Invoice ID returned by a sandbox billing flow.
Webhook event ID returned by a failed or received sandbox webhook.
Unique value for a crawl idempotency key. Use a new value when testing a fresh operation and reuse it only to test deduplication.
Razorpay HMAC signature for the exact sandbox webhook body. A placeholder is intentionally invalid.
Unique Razorpay sandbox event identifier; reuse only when testing webhook deduplication.
Destination plan ID for a subscription plan-change request.
Gross amount for the test invoice, matching the invoice being used.

Default `false`: requests must return a documented success status. Set to `true` in a Postman environment only for a deliberate negative test; then any 4xx is accepted, while the API error envelope is still checked.
Local Razorpay webhook signing secret for development/sandbox only. Keep the real value in a private Postman environment; never commit or share it.
Bearer token for an administrator test account. Obtain it with the v2 login request and copy it into a private Postman environment; never commit or share it.

Default `false`. Set to `true` in a private Postman environment only when you intentionally test destructive/state-changing operations such as delete, refund, cancel, revoke, dunning, or webhook replay.

## Crawl Url

**Request:** `POST {{baseUrl}}/api/v1/crawler/crawl`

No extended operation description was present in the checked-in OpenAPI snapshot. This entry is documented from the imported collection's route and operation name.

**Authentication:** Bearer access token from collection variable `access_token`.

### URL and parameters
Base URL: collection variable `{{baseUrl}}` = `http://localhost:5000`.
No path or query parameters.
Request headers:
- `idempotency-key: {{idempotencyKey}}` — Required by the endpoint/provider; use a valid development/sandbox value.

### Request body
Content type: `application/json`.
Current sample body fields: `url`. Replace sample values with valid development data.

### Responses
This operation is present in the imported 123-operation collection but not in the checked-in OpenAPI snapshot. Check the target server's `/swagger.json` for current status codes and schemas.

### Versioning
v1 is deprecated. Check `Deprecation`, `Sunset`, and successor `Link` response headers; use the paired v2 request for new integrations.

### Operational notes
Crawler endpoints require a Bearer token and are rate-limited. Honor `Retry-After`; cache/search behavior depends on Redis and configured web providers.

### Postman test script
Checks that the response is below HTTP 500, that any API envelope `statusCode` matches the HTTP status, and captures common IDs/tokens from successful responses. A passing script does not replace checking business state or endpoint-specific expected status codes.

### Expected status and assertions
Default expected success status: any 2xx (not listed in the checked-in OpenAPI snapshot). The Tests tab fails on any other status by default. For a deliberate negative test, set `allowClientError=true` in a private Postman environment; then the test requires a 4xx response and validates any API error envelope. Successful JSON envelopes are checked for status/success consistency, and v1 business API requests also check deprecation headers.

### Placeholder guard
Normal runs skip this request when required IDs/tokens or sample `replace-me` values are still placeholders. Check the Postman Console for the skip reason. Set `allowClientError=true` only when you deliberately want to send invalid or missing values.
